payload.headline: Meta's sales are still growing fast, but lower margins and cash flow cloud its value

summary.thesis: Meta's sales are still growing fast, but its profit margins and free cash flow fell sharply, so today's price only adds up if cash flow recovers strongly.
summary.decision: Long-term: wait for a lower price or proof that margins are recovering. Swing: wait, because the stock is stuck in a range below its falling short-term average.
summary.act_at: Watch 591.53–605.33 on the downside and 671.85 on the upside

payload.happening: META closed at 628.77, down 1.97% on the day, and was trading near 623.22 at 10:54 ET (not a close). The stock is moving sideways, below its 20-day average of 646.1, which is falling, and its 50-day average of 678.45. Today's news is about products: Instagram's AI filter tool and a reported plan from WhatsApp's new head to improve the app and its AI. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-27.
payload.business: Demand looks healthy. Sales over the last 12 months reached 241.6B, up from 189.5B, and grew 27.53%. Growth is slowing, though: sales grew 26.07% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, compared with 33.08% two quarters ago. The bigger change is in costs. The operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) fell to 32.86% from 43.23%. Free cash flow (cash left over after running the business and investing in it) fell to 28.6B from 44.8B. The free cash flow margin is only 11.86%. The filings also flag that profit per share is lagging sales and that the company missed forecasts last quarter by 29%. The company's balance sheet has also changed: it holds 11.2B in cash against 83.7B of debt, so debt now slightly exceeds cash (net cash of -1.2B), although it has 82.4B of liquidity (cash plus money it can draw on). The likely cause is heavy spending on AI infrastructure (general knowledge). What is at risk is cash generation and margins. The core ad business is not at risk based on this data: gross margin (sales minus the direct cost of delivering them) is still 81.03%. The news items, the reported $14.2M of insider sales outside pre-set plans, and eBay reportedly blocking outside AI agents mainly affect sentiment or governance. They do not change demand.

worth.text: The two valuation methods disagree because they start from different numbers. The cash-flow model (DCF) starts from this year's reduced free cash flow of 28.6B. Even in its bull case it values the stock at 521.31, with a base case of 381.85, which is well below 628.77. To justify today's price, free cash flow would need to start growing at 37.4% a year, above the model's 30% cap, which gives 480.09. The price-to-sales method compares today's price with Meta's own history. It gives a range of 475.85 to 881.21, with a middle value of 707.21. Meta trades at 6.7 times sales, close to the peer median of 6.5 and at the 38th percentile of its own past five years. Its price is 21.5 times trailing earnings. In short, the stock looks reasonable on sales but expensive on cash flow, and the gap depends on whether today's heavy spending is temporary.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow recovers toward the earlier 44.8B as spending pays off, instead of staying near 28.6B.

bull: Sales grew 27.53% over the last 12 months, to 241.6B, which is fast for a company this large.
At 6.7 times sales, the stock is near the peer median of 6.5 and at only the 38th percentile of its own 5-year range.
A gross margin of 81.03% suggests the core business is still very profitable before the new spending.
bear: The operating margin fell to 32.86% from 43.23%, so costs are growing faster than sales.
Free cash flow fell to 28.6B from 44.8B, and the price assumes 37.4% starting cash-flow growth, compared with a DCF base value of 381.85.
Sales growth slowed to 26.07% from 33.08% two quarters ago, and the company missed forecasts last quarter by 29%.

levels.what: Bottom of the most-tested support zone (7 touches). A close below it would weaken the chart.
Low end of Meta's own price-to-sales history and close to the DCF value at 30% growth. This is where value becomes clearly attractive.
Middle of the own-history price-to-sales range. Above this, the price would assume the margin recovery has already happened.

longterm.why: The business is graded C, and the price is above every DCF value. Waiting for either a lower price or evidence that margins are recovering is more defensible than buying now.

swing.why: The stock is in a range, below a falling 20-day average and its 50-day average, with resistance at 641.3–651.93 just overhead. With a typical daily move (ATR) of 23.86, there is not enough room for a trade with a sensible stop and target. A clean setup would be a hold of 591.53–605.33 or a close back above 671.85.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-01-27 come after the January 15 options expiry, which prices a 12.7% move. That report on margins and cash flow is the main catalyst, so a long-term entry makes more sense after it than before.

change_mind: Next report (2027-01-27) shows the operating margin climbing back toward 43.23% from 32.86%, or free cash flow rising back toward 44.8B.
A close below 591.53 (the bottom of the 7-touch support zone) would turn the range into a downtrend and argue for avoiding the stock.
A close above 671.85 that reclaims the 50-day average of 678.45 would make a swing entry worth considering.
